lines: Routine follow-up for chronic lung disease and recurrent wheezing since NICU discharge.
The mother reports that the child has had recurrent wheezing and difficulty breathing, especially when feeding or crying.
She also notes that the infant has had multiple respiratory infections since discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit.
The infant has been on supplemental oxygen since birth and has required several courses of systemic corticosteroids for exacerbations of his respiratory symptoms.

encounters.cc: Poor weight gain, feeding difficulties, and recurrent respiratory infections with cyanosis during feeds.

lines: Poor weight gain, feeding difficulties, and recurrent respiratory infections with cyanosis during feeds.

The patient returns for Allergy and Immunology follow-up in the setting of known 22q11.2 deletion syndrome with associated T-cell lymphopenia and chronic lung disease, having been recently evaluated by Medical Genetics for feeding difficulties and muscle twitching and by Pediatric Pulmonology for chronic lung disease management.
His mother describes that he often becomes blue when crying or feeding, and he has had two hospital admissions for pneumonia in the last month.
The mother also reports that he struggles with bottle feeding, frequently spits up, and seems to tire easily during meals.
She notes that he sweats profusely while feeding and often pauses to catch his breath.
The infant has not been growing as expected, and the mother says she worries because his clothes still fit from birth.
His mother reports that he had a seizure earlier in the week that resolved spontaneously.
The father notes that the baby seems especially vulnerable to colds and rarely improves without antibiotics.
- Complex congenital heart disease with pulmonary overcirculation
- Chronic lung disease secondary to recurrent aspiration and infections
He was born full-term after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery.
- Repair of persistent truncus arteriosus with RV-PA conduit
- Captopril 0.5 mg/kg PO three times daily
- Calcium carbonate 200 mg/kg/day PO divided three times daily
- Sodium bicarbonate 2 mEq/kg/day PO divided twice daily
- Potassium citrate 2 mEq/kg/day PO divided twice daily
When asked further, the mother explains that her brother had a “heart problem” as a child, though she is not sure of the exact diagnosis.
The family lives in a rural area, and both parents work on a dairy farm.
His temperature is normal, but his oxygen saturation is in the mid-80s on room air.
On physical exam, the child is underweight and appears fatigued.
He has a soft systolic murmur best heard at the left upper sternal border.
Examination of his face shows a small chin, low-set ears, and hypertelorism.
Further evaluation reveals diminished thymic shadow on chest imaging.
An echocardiogram shows a conotruncal defect consistent with truncus arteriosus.
Flow cytometry reveals absent T cells.
